checks: Nonempty hidden sections are compact. As the visible coordinate converges, any sequence of points from the corresponding old hidden sections has limit points only in the target section. Thus fixed closed neighborhoods eventually contain those sections and their volumes converge down to the target volume.

Brunn–Minkowski gives concavity of the hidden r-volume root for each set and superinterpolation across every specified anchored inclusion. Nonempty zero-volume sections are allowed because translating the positive part by points of such sections still gives the same lower Brunn–Minkowski bound, or all roots vanish.

Taking one common factor (c/kappa_r)^(1/r) and applying the triangle inequality establishes each inclusion of closed ball-section bodies. Orthogonal Fubini verifies both the volume identity and the measure pushforward, including q=0.

Every indicated halfspace depends on base and visible coordinates alone, including pure-base cuts and full or empty traces. It follows that the exact original cap mass scales by c. The claim is for the declared inclusions, as in b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e §4.
